# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# ADDITIONAL WITNESS RUNS (this lane, follow-up to the archived census
# above, same driver binary, direct invocation -- not part of the
# script's own stdout, recorded here for the same "witnessed, not typed"
# discipline):
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# (1) POSSESSIVE-QUANTIFIER SEMANTICS (the census above only shows `a++`
#     COMPILES; this settles what it MEANS). Pattern `(?:a++)a` (regex
#     source, valid UTF-8) against subject "aaa", --mode search --iters 1:
#
#   $ rust_regex_driver --pattern pat_poss.txt --list list_poss.tsv \
#         --mode search --iters 1
#   subject s1  match  0  3  0  3  1  0.000026750  -  -
#
#   ANSWER=match, START=0, END=3 -- the WHOLE 3-byte subject matched.
#   Under PCRE's true possessive semantics, `a++` would consume all
#   three 'a's with NO backtracking available to release one for the
#   trailing `a`, so the overall match at offset 0 would FAIL (and no
#   other offset has enough 'a's either -- the pattern would report
#   nomatch on "aaa" entirely). It did not: the crate's automaton
#   exploration found a split that gives the trailing `a` its byte,
#   exactly as `a+` (non-possessive) would. VERDICT: `a++` PARSES but
#   is NOT semantically possessive under rust-regex 1.13.1 -- expected,
#   documented crate behavior (no backtracking engine, so "possessive"
#   has no operational effect; the syntax is accepted for PCRE-pattern
#   portability only). The `possessive-quantifier` capability token is
#   WITHHELD on this finding (capability = semantics, not parse-acceptance).
#
# (2) LEFTMOST-FIRST CONVENTION WITNESS (capability_set_v1.md 7.6's "not
#     independently reproduced" flag, now cleared). Pattern `foo|foobar`
#     against subject "foobar", --mode search --iters 1:
#
#   $ rust_regex_driver --pattern pat_leftmost.txt --list list_leftmost.tsv \
#         --mode search --iters 1
#   subject s2  match  0  3  0  6  1  0.000001310  -  -
#
#   ANSWER=match, START=0, END=3 -- the FIRST alternative (`foo`) won,
#   not the longer `foobar`. CONFIRMS `perl-leftmost-first`, matching
#   the source-level finding below.
#
# (3) size_limit / dfa_size_limit DEFAULTS, confirmed against the ACTUAL
#     PINNED crate source (never memory): regex-1.13.1/src/builders.rs,
#     `impl Default for Builder`:
#       .nfa_size_limit(Some(10 * (1 << 20)))     // 10,485,760 = 10 MiB
#       .hybrid_cache_capacity(2 * (1 << 20))     // 2,097,152  = 2 MiB
#     matches `src/main.rs`'s DEFAULT_SIZE_LIMIT / DEFAULT_DFA_SIZE_LIMIT
#     constants and the driver's own printed `info size_limit 10485760`
#     / `info dfa_size_limit 2097152` lines exactly. `MatchKind::
#     LeftmostFirst` is hardcoded in `Builder::build_one_bytes()` (the
#     `regex::bytes::RegexBuilder` path this driver uses) -- confirms (2)
#     structurally, not just by one witness.
#
# (4) CROSS-CHECK against bench/capability@0.1's own `requires=` tags
#     (patterns.rxt): every one of the 22 REFUSED corpus patterns ties to
#     a withheld REQUIRES_VOCAB token by name EXCEPT `mojibake-curly-quote`
#     (requires=non-utf8-subject alone), which refuses for the SEPARATE,
#     documented I-72 pattern-source-UTF-8 reason (testees/rust/CLAUDE.md)
#     under a token this adapter declares SATISFIED -- the same
#     "documented, not a surprise" shape re2-default/onig-default/
#     tre-default/vectorscan-block-nosom precedent sets for a real corpus
#     refusal under a satisfied token.
